 Judgment

This appeal is directed against the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal in MVC No.718/2016 dated 19.04.2017, whereby, seeking enhancement of compensation on the grounds urged in the appeal memorandum.
2. This appeal is listed for hearing on application - I.A.No.1/2019.
This Court has considered the application along with the affidavit and also the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties and has allowed the application by separate order.
However, with the consent of learned counsel for the parties, this appeal is taken up for final disposal.

3. Factual matrix of this appeal is as under:-
NC: 2023:KHC:28560-DB It is transcribed in the appeal that the petitioner namely Eramma - the injured in a road traffic accident filed a petition before the Tribunal seeking compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- under the Motor Vehicles Act with interest at 12% per annum.

It is stated in her petition that on 17.03.2016, at about 5.30 p.m.,
when the petitioner after completion of her agricultural work in her land was proceeding as a pedestrian on the left side of the road, a Bolero Maxi Car bearing No.KA-16/C-3172, which was driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner,
came from back side in a high speed without observing the traffic rules and dashed the petitioner and capsized his vehicle.
As a result of which, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries on her head and caused fractures.

She was immediately shifted to District Hospital, Chitradurga, where she was provided treatment of first aid to save her life and thereafter, on the advice of the doctor, she was shifted to SSIMS Hospital,
Davanagere, where CT scan of the brain was done.

In the report of the CT Scan, it is c o n f i r m e d t h a t t h e p e t i t i o n e r h a s s u f f e r e d h e a d i n j u r y w i t h N C :

entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text: During the period of treatment, she has undergone surgeries of left and right tibia by inserting rod, screw, plates, nails and implants so also skin grafting was done.
She has taken treatment as inpatient for 58 days, from 18.03.2016 to 02.05.2016 and incurred medical expenses of Rs.2,00,000/-.
She has also taken follow up treatment as an out patient.
She is unable, to squat on the floor, her left limb below knee was amputed and later, her right limb above knee is amputed.

Because of these injuries she has suffered 100%
permanent disability.

Therefore, she filed a claim petition before the Tribunal seeking absolute compensation under the relevant provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act.
4.
Subsequent to initiation of the proceedings seeking compensation under the Act, the process had been served upon the respondents to participate in the petition.
Respondent No.1 remained absent and he was placed exparte.
Respondent No.2 namely the Manager of the ICICI Lombard General Insurance Co. Ltd., had appeared through a counsel and contested the petition by filing its detailed objections.

entities.text: ICICI Lombard General Insurance Co. Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Respondent No.2 - Insurance Company denied the entire petition averments, occurrence of the accident, injuries sustained by the injured, treatment obtained by her and so also the medical expenses spent by her.

Respondent No.2 also denied the age, occupation and earning capacity of the petitioner, who is injured and sought dismissal of the claim petition filed by the petitioner - injured as she does not deserve for such compensation and absolutely for the reasons stated therein.
Subsequent to completion of the contentions of the petitioner as well as respondent No.2, the Tribunal had formulated the issues.
The parties in order to prove their respective contentions, the injured examined herself as PW-1, a doctor as PW-2 and produced several documents marked as Exs.P.1 to P.18.

On the part of respondent No.2 - Insurance Company, no oral or documents NC:
2023:KHC:28560-DB evidence has been adduced or produced.
The Tribunal after considering the submissions made by the petitioner and respondent No.2, answered issue No.1 in the affirmative and issue No.2 in partly affirmative.

The Tribunal has recorded a finding that the petitioner/injured has proved that she had sustained injuries in the road traffic accident that occurred on 17.03.2016 at about 5.30 p.m. and also offending vehicle namely Bolero Maxi Truck bearing No.KA-16/C-3172.
The Tribunal awarded a compensation of Rs.11,62,000/- with interest at the rate of 7.5% p.a., which is to that effect is indicated in the operative portion of the order.

The petitioner - injured being not satisfied by the award passed by the Tribunal, has preferred this appeal seeking intervention of this Court and also seeking absolute compensation for the injuries suffered by her as indicated in the wound certificate.
5. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant has produced all the documentary evidence for the injuries suffered by her in the road traffic accident.
He submits that the appellant is an agriculturist by avocation and was earning Rs.3/- lakhs p.a.
Due to the road traffic accident, the appellant is suffering permanent physical disability.

In the discharge cards produced at Exs.P.10 and P.11, disability certificate at Eramma vs Icici Lombard General Ins Co. Ltd on 11 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188658826/
3 Ex.P.12, four photos of the appellant's disability at Ex.P.13, would indicate that the appellant has suffered grievous injuries.

entities.text: Eramma vs Icici Lombard General Ins Co. Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The medical bills also reveal that the appellant has spent huge money for her treatment and undergone surgeries for the same.
The appellant has undergone amputation to both legs and also has suffered 100% permanent disability.
She is unable to continue the agricultural work and has to depend on others for her livelihood.
She has lost her earning.
He would contend that the Tribunal has awarded meager compensation insofar as the injuries sustained and treatment taken by the appellant is concerned.
He also further submits that the appellant has not at all awarded any compensation towards future medical expenses, as the appellant has undergone surgeries and implants were inserted.

For the treatment NC: 2023:KHC:28560-DB of the implants,
the appellant has to undergo another surgery and follow up treatment.

As per the wound certificate at Ex.P.7, though the appellant has suffered left ear bleeding, open crush injury of lower limb of left leg and open crush injury of dorsum of the right foot, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal towards pain and sufferings, attendant charges and loss of amenities is also very meager.

The appellant was aged 55 years, earning Rs.3/- lakhs per annum and due to the injuries suffered from the accident, she is not in a position to work as she was working earlier as an agriculturist and earn for her livelihood.
He submits that the Tribunal has assessed the monthly earning of the appellant at Rs.7,000/- p.m., which is on the lower side.
As per the chart issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority at Rs.9,500/- p.m. as notional income, which is based upon certain reliance laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
He submits that the income of the appellant should be assessed reasonably.
Therefore, he seeks intervention of NC: 2023:KHC:28560-DB this Court and prays for enhancement of the compensation.

6. Sri Pradeep B., learned counsel for respondent No.1 - Insurance Company submits that the Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation to the appellant by considering the wound certificate and the income assessed is as per the avocation of the appellant.

The appellant has not produced any documents to show that the appellant was earning Rs.3/- lakhs per annum and in the absence of any proof of definite income of the appellant, the Tribunal has properly appreciated the contentions and the documents and recorded the finding at para No.15 of the judgment and has assessed the monthly income at Rs.7,000/-.
He would further submit that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal towards all the heads are proper and reasonable and does not have any ground for enhancement of compensation.
Therefore, he prays for dismissal of the appeal.

The appellant has sustained injuries in the road traffic accident that occurred on 17.03.2016,
when the appellant after completion of agricultural work was proceeding as a pedestrian on the left side of the road, the driver of the Bolero Maxi truck bearing No.KA-16/C-3172 came from back side in a rash and negligent manner with high speed without observing the traffic rules and regulations dashed the appellant.
The injuries suffered by the appellant are grievous in nature.
She was shifted to SSIMS Hospital, Davanagere.

She has undergone CT Scan of brain confirmed closed head injury with left parietal arch EDH contusion, compounded fracture of left distal 1/3rd of tibia, fracture of right distal 1/3rd of right tibia, bleeding from ear, open crush injury of lower 1/3rd of left leg dorsum Eramma vs Icici Lombard General Ins Co. Ltd on 11 August, 2023

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188658826/
4 of the right foot and other injuries all over her body.
She had undergone surgery of left and right tibia by inserting rod, screw, plates, nails were implanted and skin grafting was done.
She was admitted in the hospital from 18.03.2016 to 02.05.2016.
Both legs are amputed and has suffered 100% permanent disability.

As per Ex.P.10, which is discharge card issued from SSIMS Hospital, Davanagere, it would go to show that the appellant has sustained closed head injury EDC left parietal, fracture of right distal 1/3rd of tibia and compound fracture of distal.
Ex.P.11 is discharge card issued from Government hospital, Holalkere, where she had taken treatment from 22.12.2016 to 25.12.2016, as an inpatient.
Ex.P.13 (1 to 4) are photographs and Ex.P.14 is CD.
Ex.P.15 is the inpatient bill amounting to Rs.57,260/- and Ex.P.16 (1 to 148) are the medical bills amounting to Rs.1,86,672/-.
Ex.P.18 is the RTC extract.
Therefore, the appellant has filed this appeal seeking intervention of this Court in the judgment and award whereby, Tribunal has awarded compensation, but inadequate.
9. The appellant due to the accident is finding difficulty in walking and needs one attendant for her day- to-day requirements.
She has adduced evidence to that effect as she is an Agriculturist by cultivating the land.
It - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:28560-DB is stated in the petition that she was earning Rs.3,00,000/- per annum.
She has produced RTC extract as per Ex.P.18, which relates to Sy.No.131, which reveals that the land is measuring 2 acres 5 guntas, standing in the name of the husband of the appellant.
But the Tribunal has rightly appreciated the earning of the appellant as no material is produced by the appellant to prove her definite income.

The learned counsel for the appellant in this matter has urged seeking enhancement of compensation by intervention into the judgment and award of the Tribunal, which has assessed the notional income at Rs.7,000/- p.m., which is not just and proper.

10. In view of the afore stated facts, due to the injuries suffered by the appellant in the road traffic accident, the appellant has lost her future income and the same requires to be quantified by assessing the income at Rs.9,500/- p.m., as per the chart of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.

In view of the judgments of the Apex Court in the cases of SARLA VARMA (SMT.) AND - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:28560-DB OTHERS VS. DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION AND ANOTHER reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 and in NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED Vs. PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157, the appropriate multiplier is '11' as the appellant is aged 55 years.

5

sentences.text: the doctor has deposed 92% permanent disability, the Tribunal has taken only 75% disability, which is not just and proper.
The Tribunal has not considered the opinion of the doctor and has not properly appreciated the material on record.
It has inadequately awarded compensation of Rs.6,93,000/- only, which is not just and proper.
11. Learned counsel for the appellant has produced certain documents to show that the appellant has suffered amputation to both legs.
The documents are produced by filing I.A. No.1/2019.

Therefore,
in view of the afore - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC:28560-DB stated facts, the disability of the appellant is assessed at 100%.
The loss of future income would however, works out at Rs.13,79,400/- (9,500 + 10% x 12 x 11) instead of Rs.6,93,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
12. Due to the injuries suffered by the appellant in the road traffic accident, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.1,00,000/- towards 'pain and sufferings', which is not reasonable and proper.
Therefore, considering the injuries suffered by the appellant, Rs.2,00,000/- is awarded towards the head 'pain and sufferings'.
The appellant has suffered loss of amenities.
She has to forgo all the happiness and joy of living due to the amputation of both legs and so also that an attendant is permanently required to take care of her day-to-day requirements.
Therefore, Rs.1,50,000/- is awarded towards loss of amenities as against Rs.50,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
13. The appellant has produced in all 148 medical bills as per Ex.P.16.
The Tribunal has considered and has rightly awarded Rs.2,44,000/-.
Therefore, interference of - 15 - NC: 2023:KHC:28560-DB this Court is not called for.

However, the appellant though was admitted in the hospital from 18.03.2016 to 02.05.2016, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.25,000/- towards diet,
attendant charge and traveling expenses, which seems to be inadequate.
The appellant has undergone various surgeries and to take care of the appellant, one person has to be there a whole day.
The expenses for the attendant, food and nourishment for the appellant and the conveyance for the attendant to nurse the appellant is primary and important.
The compensation awarded by the Tribunal is not just and proper.

Therefore, an amount of Rs.75,000/- is awarded towards the head 'attendant charges, food and nourishment, conveyance etc.'
14.
Insofar as the compensation awarded by the Tribunal towards the head 'future attendant charges' is concerned, the Tribunal has awarded inadequately.

It is the submission of the learned counsel for the appellant - claimant that the appellant has to take further medical - 16 - Eramma vs Icici Lombard General Ins Co. Ltd on 11 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188658826/
6 NC: 2023:KHC:28560-DB treatment.

entities.text: Eramma vs Icici Lombard General Ins Co. Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: An attendant is must and required to assist the appellant.
The attendant requires food for nourishment and also has to spend some amount towards conveyance.
It would be difficult for the appellant to earn for the future attendant charges as she is suffering from 100% permanent disability due to amputation of both legs.
Therefore, Rs.2,00,000/- is awarded as against Rs.50,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
15. Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted by producing documents by way of filing I.A.No.1/2019.

The doctor- P.W.2 has stated in his evidence that the appellant has suffered 92.17%
permanent disability and the appellant is unable to sit, stand, move, walk, use the steps, movement of both the legs are completely restricted and unable to walk without the help of crutches and also unable to bear any weight on her both limbs.
The appellant has undergone surgeries and implants are inserted.
The Tribunal has erred in not awarding compensation towards 'future medical expenses'.
Learned - 17 - NC: 2023:KHC:28560-DB counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant has to take future treatment in view of the implants.
This Court considering all the aspects, Rs.1,00,000/- is awarded towards the head 'future medical expenses'.

16. Therefore, the claimants are entitled for following amount of compensation:
Loss of future income due to Rs. 13,79,400/-
 disabilty  Pain and sufferings Rs. 2,00,000/-
 Attendant charges, food and Rs. 75,000/-
 nourishment, conveyance etc.

Medical expenses Rs. 2,44,000/-
 Loss of amenities Rs. 1,50,000/-
 Future medical attendant Rs. 2,00,000/-
Future medical expenses Rs. 1,00,000/-
. In all, claimant is entitled for a sum of Rs.23,48,400/- as against Rs.11,62,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
The compensation is enhanced by Rs.11,86,400/-.

18. Sri. B. Pradeep, learned counsel for the respondent No.1 submits that the Tribunal has awarded - 18 - Eramma vs Icici Lombard General Ins Co. Ltd on 11 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188658826/
7 NC: 2023:KHC:28560-DB interest at the rate of 7.5% p.a., which is exorbitant.

entities.text: Eramma vs Icici Lombard General Ins Co. Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the interest aspect, this Court finds that the Tribunal has awarded 7.5% p.a.
In general, the rate of interest awarded on the compensation is 6% p.a.
Therefore, the same rate of interest i.e., 6% p.a., is awarded in this case as well.

It shall be effected from the date of petition till the date of realization excluding the compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- awarded by this Court towards the head 'future attendant charges' and Rs.1,00,000/- awarded towards the head 'future medical expenses'.

Accordingly, we proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed-in-part.
The impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal in MVC No.718/2016 dated 19.04.2017 is modified.

Claimant is entitled for compensation of Rs.23,48,400/- as against Rs.11,62,000/- awarded by the Tribunal with interest at - 19 - NC: 2023:KHC:28560-DB the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till deposit.

(ii) Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation amount with 6% interest excluding the compensation awarded under the heads 'future medical expenses' and 'future attendant charges' within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this judgment,
before the Tribunal.
